answer: Every agent identity anchors to a single vertex in a public trust graph: to join, an agent must burn a small stake and earn endorsements from established peers, so each fake identity costs real funds and real reputation. Like an ember carried down a river, trust flows only along verified edges — a Sybil cluster with no inbound links from honest agents stays isolated, its attestations worthless, while creating thousands of linked fakes would cost more in stake and endorsements than the rewards they could extract.
